title: Core knows how far the board branch is from the remote
description: Add to packages/core/src/sync.ts (reusing git.ts helpers: remoteName, refExists, isAncestor) a read that fetches the board branch and returns { ahead, behind, remote } or 'no-remote' / 'offline'. The fetch has a short timeout so an offline machine answers 'offline' instead of hanging. Under the ff-auto answer, also add a fast-forward-only pull: taken only when behind > 0, ahead === 0 and nothing uncommitted under .sober/; it takes the ADR 0025 lock like sync() does. Export through packages/core/src/index.ts and update the exports snapshot (ADR 0028 ceiling). Tests in packages/core/src/sync.test.ts (or next to it) with a bare remote: behind, ahead, diverged, no remote, and the fast-forward refused when there is local work.

brief.approach:
One read, one optional act, folded into a single exported function so `core`'s surface grows by two names and not four.

**The shape.** In `packages/core/src/sync.ts`, beside `boardTravels` (which is already the "answer a question about the remote board without touching anything" function and is the model for register and placement):

```ts
export type BoardDistance =
	| { readonly kind: 'ok'; readonly ahead: number; readonly behind: number; readonly remote: string; readonly pulled: SyncChange | null }
	| { readonly kind: 'no-remote' }
	| { readonly kind: 'offline' }

export const boardDistance = async (
	paths: Paths,
	branch: string,
	options?: { readonly pull?: boolean; readonly timeoutMs?: number },
): Promise<BoardDistance>
```

`pull` defaults to `false`, so a caller that only wants the number cannot move the branch by forgetting a flag. `pulled` is `null` unless a fast-forward was actually taken. Two names on `index.ts` (`boardDistance`, `type BoardDistance`) — see the ceiling note below.

**The read.** `remoteName(root)` null → `{ kind: 'no-remote' }`. Then fetch `+refs/heads/<branch>:refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>` exactly as the private `fetchBoard` does, but do not reuse `fetchBoard`: it throws `SoberError` for an unreachable remote, and this function's whole point is that an offline machine answers instead of throwing. Catch, and split on the same English stderr `fetchBoard` already matches (`git.ts` pins `LC_ALL: 'C'`, so this is a contract — ADR from `core-runs-git-in-english-so-its-error-te-tljx`): `couldn't find remote ref` means the remote simply has no board, which is `{ kind: 'ok', ahead: <local commits>, behind: 0 }` when the local branch exists and `{ kind: 'no-remote' }` when neither side has one; anything else is `{ kind: 'offline' }`, never a throw. If `refExists(root, branch)` is false locally, the answer is `behind: <all of theirs>, ahead: 0`.

Count with one call, not two: `git rev-list --left-right --count <branch>...<remote>/<branch>` returns `ahead\tbehind`. Parse both integers; a non-numeric line is a bug, not an offline case, so let it throw.

**The timeout.** `exec` in `packages/core/src/git.ts` calls `execFile` with no timeout, so an unreachable host hangs the session hook that will call this. Add a fourth, optional parameter to `gitWithEnv` — `options: { readonly timeoutMs?: number } = {}` — and pass `timeout: options.timeoutMs` through to `execFile`. Every existing caller passes three arguments and keeps compiling; no new export. `execFile` kills the child on timeout and the rejection arrives as a `GitError`, which the catch above turns into `{ kind: 'offline' }`. Default in `boardDistance`: 5000 ms, a named `const` beside the function with one sentence saying why a fetch that has not answered in five seconds is an offline machine and not a slow one.

**The fast-forward.** Taken only when all three hold: `behind > 0`, `ahead === 0`, and nothing uncommitted under `.sober/`. For the third, do not use `hasUncommitted(root)` — it asks about the whole working tree, and a person with an edited `src/foo.ts` has nothing to do with the board. Ask the narrow question: `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no -- .sober` is non-empty → refuse. Refusing is not a failure: the result still says `ahead`/`behind` with `pulled: null`, and the caller prints the reminder.

The pull itself is `update-ref` plus `materialize`, exactly as `adoptBoard` does it (`sync.ts`, the `update-ref refs/heads/<branch> <theirs>` then `materialize(paths, ours, theirs)` pair) — the board branch is never checked out, which is the invariant the whole file is built on. Wrap the whole function body in `withLock(paths, 'distance', ...)` the way `sync` and `resolveConflict` do, only when `pull` is true: a read that takes the writer lock would make the session hook fight every `accept`. Pass no `windows` argument; `withLock` reads the config's `lock.staleSeconds` / `lock.waitSeconds` itself.

**Export ceiling.** `packages/core/src/exports.test.ts` has `CEILING = 107` and the snapshot already holds 108 names, so `core` is one over today and the test warns rather than fails. Two more names makes it 110. Do not raise `CEILING` — ADR 0028 says the number moves by ADR and what shaves it is the deletion pass, so leave the warning standing and update only `packages/core/src/__snapshots__/exports.test.ts.snap` (`pnpm vitest run packages/core/src/exports.test.ts -u`). A reviewer seeing the warning is the alarm working, not a thing to silence.

**Tests** in a new `packages/core/src/sync.test.ts`, built the way `packages/core/src/git.test.ts` builds its pair: `tmpRoot` from `./tmp.fixture.js`, a bare repo, a work repo with `origin` pointing at it. Six cases, each naming what it protects: the remote is ahead and nothing local is unsent → `behind: N, ahead: 0` and, with `pull: true`, the records arrive and `pulled` is non-null; the local branch is ahead → `ahead: N, behind: 0` and `pull: true` changes nothing; the two have diverged → both counts non-zero and `pulled: null`; no remote at all → `no-remote`; a remote pointing at a path that does not exist → `offline` within the timeout, not a throw; the remote is ahead but `.sober/nodes/` has an uncommitted edit → `pulled: null` and the counts still correct.

Nothing outside `core` changes. The session hook (`a-session-that-opens-says-the-board-is-b-m2d6`) and the dashboard's behind-count (`the-dashboard-shows-how-far-behind-the-b-o5si`) are the two nodes that will call this; do not write either surface here.

acceptance.proves: all six distances answer correctly against a real bare remote: behind, ahead, diverged, no remote, offline-within-timeout, and the fast-forward refused when .sober/ has local work
the optional timeout parameter added to gitWithEnv broke no existing git call, and the lock still behaves as it did
the new surface is in the snapshot a reviewer reads, and the over-ceiling warning is printed rather than suppressed
the ceiling was not quietly raised to hide the two new names — ADR 0028 says that number moves by ADR
only packages/core changed: no surface, no CLI, no dashboard, no MCP tool was written here
every caller of gitWithEnv across the monorepo still compiles against the widened signature
